Page(Object object)

Register a page in the Mini Program. Accepts an Object type parameter that specifies the initial data of the page, life cycle callback, event handling functions, and so on.

Parameter

Object object

Properties Type Default Value Mandatory or Not Description Remarks
data Object Initial data of the page
onLoad Function Lifecycle Callback - Monitoring Page Loading
onShow Function Lifecycle Callback - Monitoring Page Display
onReady Function Lifecycle Callback - Initial Rendering Completed on the Listening Page
onHide Function Lifecycle Callback - Hiding the Listening Page
onUnload Function Lifecycle Callback - Uninstalling the Listening Page
onPullDownRefresh Function Monitor user pull-down action
onReachBottom Function Processing function of the page pull-up and bottom-down event
onPageScroll Function Function for processing page scrolling triggering events
onTabItemTap Function Switch the tabbar or trigger the switchTab API. The function takes effect only on the tab page.
Other Any Developers can add any function or data to the Object parameter. You can use this to access the function on the page.

Sample Code

//index.js
Page({
  data: {
    text: 'This is page data.'
  },
  onLoad: function (options) {
    // Do some initialize when page load.
  },
  onShow: function () {
    // Do something when page show.
  },
  onReady: function () {
    // Do something when page ready.
  },
  onHide: function () {
    // Do something when page hide.
  },
  onUnload: function () {
    // Do something when page close.
  },
  onPullDownRefresh: function () {
    // Do something when pull down.
  },
  onPageScroll: function () {
    // Do something when page scroll
  },

  // Event handler.
  viewTap: function () {
    this.setData(
      {
        text: 'Set some data for updating view.'
      },
      function () {
        // this is setData callback
      }
    );
  },
  customData: {
    hi: 'MINA'
  }
});

data

data indicates the initial data used for the first rendering of the page.

During page loading, data is transferred from the logic layer to the rendering layer in the form of JSON strings. Therefore, data in data must be of the type that can be converted into JSON, including character strings, numbers, Boolean values, objects, and arrays.

The rendering layer can bind data through MAML.

Sample Code

<view>{{text}}</view> <view>{{array[0].msg}}</view>

Page({
  data: {
    text: 'init data',
    array: [{ msg: '1' }, { msg: '2' }]
  }
});

Life cycle callback function

onLoad(Object query)

Triggered when the page is loaded. A page can be invoked only once. You can obtain the parameters in the path for opening the current page from the onLoad parameter.

Parameters

Name Type Description
query Object Open parameters in the path of the current page.

onShow()

Triggered when the page is displayed or the foreground is switched.

onReady()

Triggered when the page is initially rendered. A page is invoked only once, indicating that the page is ready and can interact with the view layer.

Note: For example, the API used to set GUI content, ma.setNavigationBarTitle, must be performed after onReady.

onHide()

Triggered when the page is hidden or the background is switched. For example, ma.navigateTo or bottom tab switches to other pages, Mini Program switches to the background, etc.

onUnload()

Triggered when the page is unloaded. such as ma.redirectTo or ma.navigateBack to other pages.

Page Event Processing Function

onPullDownRefresh()

Listens to the user pull-down refresh event.

  • Enable the enablePullDownRefresh function in the window option of app.json or on the page configuration.
  • You can call ma.startPullDownRefresh to trigger pull-down refresh. After the call is invoked, the pull-down refresh animation is triggered. The effect is the same as that of manually pull-down refresh.
  • After data refresh is processed, the ma.stopPullDownRefresh command stops the refresh of the current page.

onReachBottom()

Monitors the user pull-up and bottom-down event.

  • You can set the trigger distance onReachBottomDistance in the window option of app.json or page configuration.
  • This event will only be triggered once during sliding within the trigger distance.
  • When onReachBottomDistance is 0, the default value is 50.

onPageScroll(Object object)

Listens to the user slide page event.

Object object:

Properties Type Description
scrollTop Number Vertical scrolling distance of the page (unit: px)

Note: Only define this method in the page when needed, and do not define an empty method. To reduce the impact of unnecessary event dispatches on the rendering layer-logic layer communication.

Note: Do not perform operations such as setData frequently in onPageScroll that may cause communication between the logic layer and the rendering layer. In particular, a large amount of data is transmitted each time, which affects communication time.

onTabItemTap(Object object)

Switch the tabbar or trigger the switchTab API.

Parameter Object object:

Attribute Type Description
index String Serial number of the clicked tab item, starting from 0.
pagePath String Page path of the clicked tabItem
text String Button text of the clicked tabItem

Sample Code:

Page({
    onTabItemTap(item) {
        console.log(item.index)
        console.log(item.pagePath)
        console.log(item.text)
    }
})

Component event processing function

You can also define component event processing functions in Page. Add event binding to components of the rendering layer. When an event is triggered, the event processing function defined in the page is executed.

Sample Code

<view bindtap="viewTap"> click me </view>

Page({
  viewTap: function () {
    console.log('view tap');
  }
});

Page.route

Path to the current page. The value is of the String type.

Page({
  onShow: function () {
    console.log(this.route);
  }
});

Page.prototype.setData(Object data)

The setData function is used to send data from the logical layer to the view layer (asynchronously) while changing the value of the corresponding this.data (synchronously).

Parameter Description

Field Type Mandatory or Not Description
data Object Yes The data to be changed this time

Object is represented in key:value format. The value corresponding to the key in this.data is changed to value.

The key can be given in the form of a data path. An item in an array or an attribute of an object can be changed, for example, array[2].message and a.b.c.d. The key does not need to be predefined in this.data.

Note:

  1. Modifying this.data without invoking this.setData cannot change the page status and result in data inconsistency.
  2. Only the data that can be JSON can be set.
  3. The amount of data set at a time cannot exceed 1024 KB. Avoid setting too many data at a time.
  4. Do not set the value of any item in data to undefined. Otherwise, this item will not be set and some potential problems may be left.

Sample code:

Sample code:

<!--index.maml-->
<view>{{text}}</view>
<button bindtap="changeText">Change normal data</button>
<view>{{num}}</view>
<button bindtap="changeNum">Change normal num</button>
<view>{{array[0].text}}</view>
<button bindtap="changeItemInArray">Change Array data</button>
<view>{{object.text}}</view>
<button bindtap="changeItemInObject">Change Object data</button>
<view>{{newField.text}}</view>
<button bindtap="addNewField">Add new data</button>

// index.js
Page({
  data: {
    text: 'init data',
    num: 0,
    array: [{ text: 'init data' }],
    object: {
      text: 'init data'
    }
  },
  changeText: function () {
    // this.data.text = 'changed data' // Do not modify it directly. this.data
    // Should be using setData
    this.setData({
      text: 'changed data'
    });
  },
  changeNum: function () {
    // Alternatively, you can use setData to set the modified fields immediately after modifying this.data.
    this.data.num = 1;
    this.setData({
      num: this.data.num
    });
  },
  changeItemInArray: function () {
    // For an object or array field, you can directly modify a subfield below it, which is usually better than modifying the entire object or array.
    this.setData({
      'array[0].text': 'changed data'
    });
  },
  changeItemInObject: function () {
    this.setData({
      'object.text': 'changed data'
    });
  },
  addNewField: function () {
    this.setData({
      'newField.text': 'new data'
    });
  }
});
